components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main call-to-action. Used for vault creation, unlock, confirm actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; background: #3b82f6; color: #f4f4f5; border: none; border-radius: 6px; padding: 8px 16px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms ease-in-out; outline: none; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #2563eb; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3b82f6; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary actions, cancel buttons, toolbar icon buttons.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; background: transparent; color: #a1a1aa; border: none; border-radius: 6px; padding: 8px 16px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 400; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms ease-in-out, color 150ms ease-in-out; outline: none; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: #27272a; color: #f4f4f5; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3b82f6; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Delete confirmations. Never used as a primary CTA.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; background: #ef4444; color: #f4f4f5; border: none; border-radius: 6px; padding: 8px 16px; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms ease-in-out; outline: none; } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background: #dc2626; } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ef4444; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Password fields, label inputs, search fields.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; background: #3f3f46; color: #f4f4f5; border: 1px solid #52525b; border-radius: 6px; padding: 8px 12px; font-size: 14px; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; outline: none; transition: border-color 150ms ease-in-out, box-shadow 150ms ease-in-out; box-sizing: border-box; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #a1a1aa; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #3b82f6; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(59,130,246,0.3); } .ds-input.error { border-color: #ef4444; }

narrative.overview:
LockBox is designed to feel like a quiet, secure place — a room you return to that's always exactly as you left it. The interface doesn't announce itself. It asks nothing of your attention beyond the task at hand. When you open it to find a credential, you should feel immediate calm: this is a tool that respects what it's protecting.

The palette is deep graphite — not blue-black or warm charcoal, but the flat, matte dark of slate or gunmetal. Surfaces layer from near-black through three graphite steps to the interactive foreground. Blue-500 is the only saturated color and earns its presence only at moments of action: the primary button, focus rings, active states.

The system explicitly rejects: the glossy gradients and glow effects of 'security theater' UI; the cramped, terminal-gray aesthetic of developer-spartan tools; and the corporate-blue corporate password manager look.
keyCharacteristics: Deep graphite dark mode — no warm tint, no blue-black, no glassmorphism
Single saturated accent (blue-500) used only for action and focus
System font stack — no external font requests, no network
14px body, 12px labels; hierarchy through weight contrast not size explosion
150ms transitions on interactive elements — smooth, never flashy
Modals always have focus traps; credentials always masked by default
Flat surfaces at rest — no ambient shadows in the resting state

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue is reserved for one role: action and focus. #3b82f6 does not appear on decorative borders, section headers, or hover backgrounds. Its rarity is its authority.

rules.name: The Graphite Layering Rule
rules.body: Every surface step up in elevation uses exactly one step up the zinc ramp: base (#18181b) → surface (#27272a) → elevated (#3f3f46) → interactive (#52525b). Don't skip steps.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is communicated by changing weight (400→500) before changing size. Don't reach for a larger font size when 500 weight at 14px will establish the hierarchy.

rules.name: The No-External-Fonts Rule
rules.body: No Google Fonts, no Typekit, no CDN font imports. System fonts only. Every external request is a potential leak vector in a security tool.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow at rest. Hover states use background color fill. Shadows are reserved for genuinely floating surfaces (modals, context menus).

dos: Do use the graphite ramp sequentially: base → surface → elevated → interactive
Do reserve Action Blue (#3b82f6) for interactive elements only: primary buttons, focus rings, active states
Do always show credential values as 16 bullets by default
Do apply 150ms transitions on background-color, color, and opacity for all interactive state changes
Do trap focus in every modal — first focusable element receives focus on open
Do use ring-2 ring-blue-500 focus rings on all keyboard-navigable elements
Do use position: fixed for context menus and dropdowns
donts: Don't use glassmorphism (backdrop-filter + opacity overlays as a design choice)
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe
Don't add drop shadows to resting surfaces
Don't vary the credential mask length with actual value length — always 16 bullets
Don't use blue (#3b82f6) for decorative purposes
Don't use the corporate-blue credential manager aesthetic
Don't use motion-heavy entrances or parallax effects
Don't show any credential value by default on any surface
